metadata.purpose: Ground-truth test cases for validating the interaction-risk reasoning prompt, per the Week 2-3 task 'test prompts against known interaction pairs to validate output quality before scaling up'.
metadata.how_to_use: Run each case through test_harness.py. Categories documented_major/moderate/minor are the 'known interaction pairs' (positive ground truth, taken directly from the reference guide). negative_control cases must NOT trigger a false positive. edge_* cases probe specific reasoning behaviors the prompt is designed to handle.

test_cases.notes: Ketorolac + enoxaparin, direct documented pair.
Ketorolac + another NSAID, group-documented pair.
Oral NSAID + enoxaparin.
Domperidone + miconazole, QT prolongation risk.

Both are combination products — this case also tests that the model decomposes BOTH into active ingredients (Codeine from 123 Cold & Flu; Chlorpheniramine from Congestal) rather than treating them as opaque single entities.
Metronidazole + enoxaparin.
NSAID + insulin, glucose effect.
Streptoquin decomposes to include streptomycin; Ketofan is ketoprofen — nephrotoxic potential pair.
Opposing GI motility effects.
PPI reduces absorption of oral antifungal.
Antacid binding reduces absorption of other oral drugs.
Codeine (from combo product) vs. domperidone — also a decomposition test.
Theoretical antiplatelet activity of proteolytic enzymes.
Vitamin C / gastric pH.
Lactulose transit-time effect on absorption of another oral medicine, applied to a specific example.
Second-generation antihistamine, low QT risk vs. domperidone.
Two topical, locally-acting products with no documented or plausible systemic overlap. Model must NOT invent an interaction.
Both herbal, both listed as low-interaction-potential; not a documented pair.
Vitamin B-complex + antihistamine, unrelated mechanisms.
Throat lozenge (local) + antihistamine.

None of Congestal's three ingredients (paracetamol, chlorpheniramine, pseudoephedrine) have a documented insulin interaction. Pseudoephedrine's mild sympathomimetic effect on glucose is a real but minor, textbook-level consideration — a NONE_KNOWN or a clearly-flagged MINOR/inferred is acceptable; anything MODERATE+ or asserted as verified is a fail. This case checks the model doesn't over-infer.

Nexium is NOT in the reference guide's 42-product catalog — simulates a newly stocked item the interaction database hasn't been manually reviewed for yet, even though inventory/lookup already knows it. Esomeprazole is the same class (PPI) as pantoprazole (Controloc), which IS documented against miconazole as MODERATE. The model should reach the same severity by class analogy and explicitly mark it as inferred, not verified.

Three-product basket. Only one pairwise combination (codeine vs. domperidone) has a documented finding; Duphalac shouldn't contribute a false positive. Tests correct aggregation to a single highest_severity across many candidate pairs.
A single combination product with no comparator. The model must NOT flag its own co-formulated ingredients (paracetamol/chlorpheniramine/pseudoephedrine) as interacting with each other.

'Congestin 500' does not exist in the catalog (deliberately similar to the real 'Congestal' to test the model doesn't silently guess a fuzzy match). Model should report it as unresolved rather than assuming an identity.
